question.text: Which of the following is a key feature of the F&O trading system?

answer.text: It provides a fully automated screen-based order-driven market with price-time priority
It allows negotiated deals between known counterparties
It operates on an open-outcry system
It matches orders based solely on time priority

explanation.text: The Logic: The F&O trading system is a fully automated screen-based, order-driven market (workbook pages 128 and 131-132). Orders are matched on price-time priority — the best price gets first preference, and among orders at the same price, the one entered earlier is matched first. The Trap: Open-outcry systems are old pit-based trading methods and are not used in Indian exchange-traded derivatives. Negotiated deals between known counterparties are characteristic of OTC markets, not the F&O trading system. Matching is on price-time priority, not on time alone. Note: Price-time priority is a universal matching principle for order-driven exchange systems.
